question.problem:
The charge $q(t),$ in coulombs, and current $I(t),$ in amperes, in a series RCL circuit are related by the equation

$$
\frac{dI}{dt}+9I+18q=25.
$$

Find an equation for the current in the circuit, expressing your answer in terms of time $t$ (in seconds) only, and given that the initial charge on the capacitor is $\frac{1}{6}\,\text{C}$ and the initial current is $\frac{5}{4}\,\text{A}.$
question.worked_solution:
The current $I,$ measured in amperes, is defined as the rate of flow of charge $q,$ measured in coulombs.

$$
I=\frac{dq}{dt}
$$

Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t,$ the differential equation governing the current in the circuit is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{d}{dt}(\frac{dI}{dt}+9I+18q) & =\frac{d}{dt}(25) \\ \frac{{d}^{2}I}{d{t}^{2}}+9\,\frac{dI}{dt}+18\,\frac{dq}{dt} & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

which, when substituting in $I=\frac{dq}{dt},$ gives

$$
\frac{{d}^{2}I}{d{t}^{2}}+9\,\frac{dI}{dt}+18I=0.
$$

The given equation is a second-order linear homogeneous equation with constant coefficients. To find the general solution, we must take a linear combination of two linearly independent solutions.

Assuming the solutions take the form $I={e}^{\lambda t},$ we obtain two solutions, namely, $I={e}^{-6t}$ and $I={e}^{-3t}.$
So, the general solution in our case is

$$
I(t)=A{e}^{-6t}+B{e}^{-3t}.
$$

We're told that the circuit starts with an initial charge of $\frac{1}{6}\,\text{C}$ on the capacitor and an initial current of $\frac{5}{4}\,\text{A}.$
Now, solving the given relation for $\frac{dI}{dt},$ we have

$$
\frac{dI}{dt}=25-9I-18q.
$$

So, we can apply the initial conditions $I(0)=\frac{5}{4}$ and 

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}^{′}(0) & =25-9I(0)-18q(0) \\  & =25-9\cdot \frac{5}{4}-18\cdot \frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{43}{4},\end{aligned}
$$

and solve for $A$ and $B.$

- Substituting $I(0)=\frac{5}{4}$ into our general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4} & =A{e}^{-6(0)}+B{e}^{-3(0)} \\ \frac{5}{4} & =A+B.\end{aligned}
$$

- Differentiating $I,$ we get

$$
{I}^{′}=-6A{e}^{-6t}-3B{e}^{-3t}
$$

Substituting in ${I}^{′}(0)=\frac{43}{4}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{43}{4} & =-6A{e}^{-6(0)}-3B{e}^{-3(0)} \\ \frac{43}{4} & =-6A-3B.\end{aligned}
$$

Putting the two equations in $A$ and $B$ together gives the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4}=A+B \\ \frac{43}{4}=-6A-3B\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $A=-\frac{29}{6}$ and $B=\frac{73}{12}.$ Therefore, the equation for the current (in amperes) in the circuit is

$$
I(t)=-\frac{29}{6}{e}^{-6t}+\frac{73}{12}{e}^{-3t}.
$$
